Tax Law

Maastricht University

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

Maastricht Tax Law combines Dutch and international taxation with private, administrative, constitutional and criminal law. Students learn to interpret legislation, analyse tax cases, produce legal documents and undertake individual legal research. The first year is shared with the Law bachelor.

UCR offers useful comparative law, public economics, accounting, finance and ethics. These courses do not provide the sustained tax legislation, tax procedure and tax-law methods that define this degree. We therefore show the verified Maastricht curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

All 180 EC are compulsory. The 10-EC thesis is assessed individually; the current thesis course requires at least 60 bachelor EC and a research proposal before supervision. Course prerequisites and professional-skills portfolio and participation requirements apply. There is no blanket attendance rule, though assessments can require presence. First-year study advice requires 40 EC. Optional honours and research extensions are separate from this standard pathway.
